title: India Food & Culture Tour: Delhi, Amritsar, Lucknow, Indore, Ahmedabad, Rajkot and Mumbai
meta_title: India Food & Culture Tour 15 Days: Delhi to Mumbai
meta_description: 15-day India food and culture tour: Old Delhi, the Golden Temple langar, Lucknow, Indore's Sarafa, Gujarati thalis in Rajkot and Mumbai's khau gallis.
tagline: Seven cities, seven kitchens, from Paranthe Wali Gali to Mumbai's khau gallis
facts: Delhi, Amritsar, Lucknow, Indore, Ahmedabad, Rajkot, Mumbai
Train to Amritsar, 4 short flights, 1 drive
intro: A journey through India by its plate. Each city gives you its signature kitchen and the monuments and markets that explain it: Mughal Delhi, Sikh Amritsar, Nawabi Lucknow, the night food market of Indore, Gandhi's Ahmedabad, our home town of Rajkot, and Mumbai's Irani cafés and street stalls. We changed two days of the original plan: Delhi to Amritsar is now a morning train instead of a nine-hour drive, and Somnath, about four hours from Rajkot each way, is an optional overnight instead of a day trip.
highlights: Paranthe Wali Gali, Khari Baoli spice market and the Red Fort in Old Delhi
State canteens of Andhra and Odisha, and Dilli Haat's regional food stalls
The Golden Temple, its langar kitchen that serves tens of thousands a day, and the Partition Museum
Lucknow's Imambaras, chikankari workshops and basket chaat
Mandu's Afghan palaces and Indore's Sarafa night market
Kathiyawadi breakfast and a royal lunch at Gondal, then Mumbai's Parsi cafés and Juhu beach

days.title: Connaught Place and a first taste of Delhi
days.summary: Arrival, Connaught Place and dinner at Moti Mahal.
strip: Airport to Connaught Place about 45 minutes

rows.label: On arrival
rows.title: Meet your driver
rows.text: With a name sign at the airport.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Connaught Place
rows.text: Colonial arcades in a double ring of shops and cafés.

rows.label: Afternoon · United Coffee House
rows.title: Coffee and snacks at a 1942 café
rows.text: Order the Cona coffee and vegetable cutlets.

rows.label: Evening · Moti Mahal, Daryaganj
rows.title: Dinner where butter chicken was born
rows.text: Meat-eaters order the butter chicken; vegetarians the dal makhani and shahi paneer, which are just as famous.

days.note: Delhi evenings in December and January are about 8° to 10° and smoggy. Bring a light jacket and a mask.

days.title: Old Delhi: parathas, the Red Fort and the spice market
days.summary: Old Delhi food walk, Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Khari Baoli and New Delhi's landmarks.
strip: Old Delhi on foot and by rickshaw

rows.label: About 08:30 · Paranthe Wali Gali
rows.title: Breakfast of stuffed parathas
rows.text: Fried parathas with potato, paneer or lentil filling, pickles and curd. All the shops here are vegetarian.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Red Fort
rows.text: The Mughal palace of 1648. Enter by the Lahori Gate.
notes: Closed on Mondays. Buy tickets online to skip the queue.

rows.label: Late morning
rows.title: Jama Masjid
rows.text: India's largest mosque; climb the south minaret for the view.
notes: Cover arms and legs; women are given a robe at the gate. Closed to visitors at prayer times.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Khari Baoli spice market
rows.text: Asia's largest spice market, by cycle rickshaw.
notes: The lanes are packed. Keep your bag in front and phone in a zipped pocket.

rows.label: Lunch · Andhra Bhavan canteen
rows.title: Andhra thali
rows.text: Unlimited vegetarian thali served on a steel plate.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: India Gate and Kartavya Path
rows.text: Drive past Rashtrapati Bhavan and the National War Memorial.

rows.label: Evening · Jama Masjid lanes
rows.title: Old Delhi dinner
rows.text: Karim's for meat-eaters; vegetarians go to Haldiram's in Chandni Chowk or the jalebi at Old Famous Jalebi Wala.

days.note: Old Delhi is best before noon. Wear closed shoes: the lanes are wet and crowded.

days.title: Akshardham, Dilli Haat and Hauz Khas
days.summary: Swaminarayan Akshardham, lunch at Dilli Haat and an evening in Hauz Khas.

rows.label: Morning · Odisha Bhavan canteen
rows.title: Odia breakfast
rows.text: Pakhala (fermented rice) and dalma, a lentil and vegetable stew.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Swaminarayan Akshardham
rows.text: A carved pink sandstone and marble temple complex.
notes: Closed on Mondays. Phones, cameras and bags are not allowed and must be deposited at the cloakroom.

rows.label: Lunch · Dilli Haat, INA
rows.title: Regional food stalls
rows.text: Each state has a stall: try Rajasthani dal baati or Bengali vegetable chop.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Hauz Khas village and lake
rows.text: A 14th-century madrasa and tank, now surrounded by boutiques and cafés.

days.note: Tomorrow's train leaves early. We pack breakfast for you, and the driver collects you at 06:30.

days.title: Morning train to Amritsar and the Golden Temple at night
days.summary: Shatabdi or Vande Bharat train to Amritsar and an evening at the Golden Temple.
strip: Palki Sahib ceremony about 21:30 to 22:00 in winter

rows.label: About 07:00 · New Delhi station
rows.title: Board the train to Amritsar
rows.text: Meals are served on board.
notes: Be on the platform 30 minutes early. Bags are scanned at the entrance.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Check in near the Golden Temple
rows.text: Rest.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple)
rows.text: Walk around the sarovar as the lights come on, and stay for the Palki Sahib ceremony, when the Guru Granth Sahib is carried to rest.
notes: Cover your head (scarves are given at the gate), remove shoes and socks, wash your feet. No tobacco or alcohol.

days.note: We changed this day from a drive to the train: Delhi to Amritsar by road is about 450 km and 9 hours, which would leave no time for the temple.

days.title: Langar, the Partition Museum and the Attari border
days.summary: Langar at the Golden Temple, the Partition Museum, kulchas and the Attari-Wagah border ceremony.

rows.label: Morning · Guru Ram Das Langar
rows.title: Langar at the Golden Temple
rows.text: Sit on the floor with thousands of others for a simple vegetarian meal. You can help in the kitchen.
meal: Free, offered by the gurdwara; a donation is welcome

rows.label: Late morning · Town Hall
rows.title: Partition Museum
rows.text: Letters, objects and voices from 1947.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Jallianwala Bagh
rows.text: The memorial garden of 1919, beside the temple.

rows.label: Afternoon · Attari
rows.title: Beating Retreat ceremony
rows.text: The flag-lowering ceremony at the border.
notes: Since May 2025 the ceremony has run in a reduced form, without the handshake and with the gates closed. We check the status the day before.

rows.label: Evening · Kesar Da Dhaba
rows.title: Punjabi dinner
rows.text: A pure-vegetarian dhaba from 1916: dal, paneer, parathas and phirni in clay bowls.

days.note: Try an Amritsari kulcha with chole for breakfast or lunch. Kulcha Land on Ranjit Avenue is a local favourite.

days.title: Fly to Lucknow, the city of Nawabs
days.summary: Flight to Lucknow and an evening at the Bara and Chota Imambara.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Flight Amritsar to Lucknow
rows.text: Usually direct.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Bara Imambara and the Bhool Bhulaiya
rows.text: A 1784 hall with no beams, and a maze on the roof. Go with a licensed guide.
notes: Remove shoes at the entrance; dress modestly.

rows.label: Late afternoon
rows.title: Chota Imambara
rows.text: Chandeliers and the Husainabad clock tower.

rows.label: Evening · Aminabad
rows.title: Lucknowi dinner
rows.text: Wahid or Tunday Kababi for meat-eaters; vegetarians try Royal Café's basket chaat in Hazratganj.

days.note: Lucknow manners are famous. 'Pehle aap' (after you) is the city's motto.

days.title: La Martinière and the chikankari workshops
days.summary: La Martinière, the chikankari market of Chowk and an evening in Hazratganj.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: La Martinière College
rows.text: The palace of Major-General Claude Martin, now a school. Visits from outside, or inside with prior permission.

rows.label: Late morning · Chowk
rows.title: Chikankari workshops
rows.text: Watch the white-on-white embroidery being stitched by hand.
notes: Buy chikankari kurtas and saris in Chowk or at government emporiums in Hazratganj.

rows.label: Evening · Hazratganj
rows.title: Free evening
rows.text: Prakash Kulfi in Aminabad for kulfi falooda.

days.note: Shops in old Lucknow close on Sundays.

days.title: Fly to Indore and a thali lunch
days.summary: Flight to Indore, thali lunch and 56 Dukaan in the evening.
strip: Flight about 1 hour 30 minutes, often via Delhi or Mumbai

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Flight Lucknow to Indore
rows.text: Check in on arrival.

rows.label: Lunch · Guru Kripa
rows.title: Malwa thali
rows.text: Dal bafla and seasonal vegetables.

rows.label: Evening · 56 Dukaan
rows.title: Street snacks
rows.text: Poha-jalebi, khopra pattice and dahi vada. Most of Indore's food is vegetarian.

days.note: Indore is India's cleanest city, eight years running. Bins are everywhere: use them.

days.title: Mandu's Afghan palaces and Sarafa night market
days.summary: Day trip to Mandu and the Sarafa night food market.
strip: About 100 km each way, 2 hours 30 minutes

rows.label: About 08:00
rows.title: Drive to Mandu
rows.text: Over the Vindhya hills.

rows.label: Late morning
rows.title: Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal and Hoshang Shah's tomb
rows.text: 15th-century Afghan palaces between two lakes.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Rani Roopmati's Pavilion
rows.text: Views over the Narmada plains, then the drive back.

rows.label: From about 21:00 · Sarafa Bazaar
rows.title: Night food market
rows.text: When the jewellers close, food stalls open: bhutte ka kees, garadu and malpua.
notes: Garadu is fried yam, not suitable for Jain diets. Ask for bhutte ka kees instead.

days.note: Mandu is lovely in the monsoon, but hot from April to June.

days.title: Fly to Ahmedabad: Gandhi's ashram and Manek Chowk
days.summary: Flight to Ahmedabad, Sabarmati Ashram, the riverfront and Manek Chowk.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Flight Indore to Ahmedabad
rows.text: Check in on arrival.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Sabarmati Ashram
rows.text: Gandhi's home from 1917 to 1930.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Sabarmati Riverfront and Atal Bridge
rows.text: A walk at sunset.

rows.label: From about 20:00 · Manek Chowk
rows.title: Night food square

days.note: Gujarat is a dry state. Food everywhere is vegetarian-friendly.

days.title: Drive to Rajkot, our home town
days.summary: Drive to Rajkot, lunch at Saraza and an evening of Rajkot street food.

rows.label: About 07:30
rows.title: Drive to Rajkot
rows.text: Breakfast at a highway Kathiyawadi stop.

rows.label: Lunch · Saraza
rows.title: Modern Gujarati lunch
rows.text: A Rajkot restaurant blending traditional and contemporary Gujarati cooking.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Snack factory visit (by arrangement)
rows.text: See how Rajkot's famous farsan snacks are made, when a visit can be arranged.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Rajkot street food
rows.text: Ghughra, chaat and Rajkot's chikki and ice-cream.

days.note: Rajkot's shops close for an afternoon rest, about 13:00 to 16:00. Plan shopping for the evening.

days.title: Gathiya-jalebi and a royal lunch in Gondal
days.summary: Kathiyawadi breakfast, Gondal palaces and a royal lunch, and a Kathiyawadi thali dinner.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Gathiya and jalebi breakfast
rows.text: Rajkot's classic breakfast at a street-side farsan shop.

rows.label: Late morning · Gondal
rows.title: Naulakha Palace and the vintage car collection
rows.text: The 17th-century palace of the Gondal royal family, and its cars and carriages.

rows.label: Midday · Gondal
rows.title: Royal lunch
rows.text: A traditional Kathiyawadi meal at the Orchard or Riverside Palace, by arrangement.

rows.label: Evening · Rajkot
rows.title: Thakkar thali
rows.text: Bajra rotla, kadhi, sev tameta and chaas.

days.note: Somnath is about 190 km from Rajkot, four hours each way. If you would like to see the evening aarti, add one night in Somnath.

days.title: Fly to Mumbai: Colaba and a khau galli
days.summary: Flight to Mumbai, Leopold Café, Colaba Causeway and a khau galli dinner.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Flight Rajkot to Mumbai
rows.text: From Rajkot's new Hirasar airport.

rows.label: Lunch · Leopold Café, Colaba
rows.title: A Colaba institution from 1871
rows.text: Vegetarian sandwiches and fresh lime soda.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Colaba Causeway
rows.text: Street shopping.
notes: Agree prices before buying and watch for pickpockets.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Khau galli dinner
rows.text: Vada pav, pav bhaji and bhel at Ghatkopar's khau galli (vegetarian) or Mohammed Ali Road (meat).

days.note: Mumbai traffic is slow. Allow an hour between Colaba and Ghatkopar.

days.title: Irani cafés and a South Mumbai heritage walk
days.summary: Kyani & Co. breakfast, a heritage walk, lunch at Britannia, Marine Drive and Juhu beach.

rows.label: Morning · Kyani & Co.
rows.title: Irani café breakfast
rows.text: Bun maska, chai and mawa cake.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Heritage walk
rows.text: Gateway of India, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, the Fort precinct and the Kala Ghoda art district with a guide.

rows.label: Lunch · Britannia & Co., Ballard Estate
rows.title: Parsi lunch
rows.text: Famous for berry pulao; vegetarians order the veg berry pulao and caramel custard.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Marine Drive
rows.text: Walk the Queen's Necklace.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Juhu beach
rows.text: Pani puri, bhel and pav bhaji at the beach stalls.

days.note: Eat at the busiest stalls and choose dry snacks if your stomach is tired after two weeks.

seasons: Cool north, warm west. Delhi fog can delay early trains in late December and January.
Very hot in the north, then monsoon.

faqs.q: Is this tour suitable for vegetarians and Jains?
faqs.a: Yes. Every stop has pure-vegetarian options, and most of the food in Indore, Ahmedabad and Rajkot is vegetarian. For Jain diets we name what to avoid, such as potato in parathas and garadu in Indore.
By road it is about 450 km and 9 hours. The Shatabdi or Vande Bharat takes about 6 hours, with meals, and leaves the evening free for the Golden Temple.

faqs.q: Can we add Somnath and Dwarka?
faqs.a: Yes. Add one night in Somnath for the evening aarti, or two nights to include Dwarka, after Rajkot.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

price_note: Contact us for a personalised quote for your dates, flights and hotel choice.
entry: Aadhaar, passport, driving licence or voter ID for flights, trains and hotel check-in
Tourist e-Visa applied online before travel
Most ASI monuments sell tickets online and by UPI at the gate
About INR 20 to 50 for Indians, more for foreigners
entry_notes: Carry the original photo ID, not a photocopy. Security at airports and many temples checks it.
Phone and internet: Jio and Airtel work best across most of this route. Download offline Google Maps before hill or forest stretches, where signal drops.

good_to_know.title: UPI, cards and cash
good_to_know.text: UPI works almost everywhere, even at small stalls. Keep some cash in INR 100 and 200 notes for temples, parking, tips and places where the network is weak.

good_to_know.title: Temple and shrine etiquette
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes where asked, and carry socks for hot stone floors. Leather belts and bags are not allowed inside some Jain and Hindu temples. Ask before photographing people and inside shrines.

good_to_know.title: Water and street food
good_to_know.text: Drink sealed bottled or filtered water only. Choose busy stalls where food is cooked in front of you, and skip cut fruit and ice from roadside stalls.

good_to_know.title: Driving times
good_to_know.text: Indian roads are slower than the kilometres suggest: plan on 40 to 50 km an hour on highways and much less in hills and towns. Your driver's breaks and meal stops are built into the timings.

good_to_know.title: Plugs and tipping
good_to_know.text: Plugs are Indian three-pin and two-pin, 230 volts. Tipping drivers and guides about INR 300 to 500 a day is appreciated.

dining_intro: India is the easiest country in the world for vegetarian and Jain travellers. We send your dietary brief to every hotel, and your driver knows clean, pure-vegetarian restaurants on each road day.
dining_avoid: Ask for food cooked fresh and tell the kitchen clearly if you eat Jain: no onion, garlic, ginger, potato or other root vegetables. Many dishes start with an onion-garlic base even when the menu says vegetarian.
food_card: Hum shuddh shakahari (Jain) hain. Pyaz, lahsun, adrak, aloo, gajar ya koi bhi zameen ke neeche ki sabzi nahi. Ande nahi. Kripya taaza banaiye. Dhanyavaad.
